messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT • Dedicated pool 'orchid-enterprise' — GPU saturation detected (100% GPU util across pool). Severity: P1. Paging oncall. metric_link: https://dash.redwood/orchid/metrics
ari-oncall: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Seeing long queue times and increased 503s from tenant orchidsvc-prod. Can anyone confirm if autoscaler fired?
tessa-sre: Checking autoscaler logs now. Autoscaler received spike but did not allocate because tenant hit reserved_capacity_limit (pool max configured = 64 GPUs, tenant commit = 56). There are 2 GPUs free but they are fragmented across nodes, scheduling failing due to topology constraints.
mohit-platform: Confirmed fragmentation. Also seeing a recent weight change for tenant priority set to "high" yesterday — shouldn't block burst but might affect placement.
nina-se: Quick customer impact note: Orchidsvc-prod handles scheduled batch reranks and low-latency inference for payments. They report increased latency and some failed requests. SE has support ticket #INC-7446.
ari-oncall: Options: 1) Manual burst: grant N GPUs from spare pool (requires billing approval + infra ops). 2) Evict low-priority/best-effort jobs from this dedicated pool to free contiguous slots. 3) Model fallback: route some traffic to a quantized variant in a different pool/region (potential quality delta). 4) Canary split: divert a % of traffic to hosted fallback while we stabilize. Thoughts?
raj-sales: We need to loop in accounts for cost approval if manual burst is used. Raj here — I can call the AE but need time. If we can evict best-effort now that's faster.
ops-jen: I can start eviction of non-prod/ci jobs tagged with "best-effort" in orchard pool. Will coordinate with infra. Doing a fast scan for candidates.
tessa-sre: Evictions look safe for ~8 GPUs (ci/bench jobs). That will likely reduce fragmentation too. Recommend: evict best-effort 8 GPUs + enable temporary placement relaxation for 15m to allow bin-packing of remaining pods.
mohit-platform: Placement relaxation requires a config flip on the scheduler. I can do that but need 2-person approval for risk. Ari + Tessa ok to proceed?
ari-oncall: I approve. Tessa?
tessa-sre: Approving. Do it. I'll monitor.
mohit-platform: Applying placement_relaxation=true -> roll started. CLI: 
```
redwoodctl scheduler set --pool orchid-enterprise --placement-relaxation=true --reason "emergency binpack"
```
ops-jen: Eviction kicks off now. Reaped 8 GPUs from bench jobs. Pods being rescheduled.
ari-oncall: Queues dropping from 600 -> 120ms p95 -> moving in right direction. 503s still present but at lower rate.
nina-se: Customer note: I've messaged Orchidsvc support channel: "We're aware of elevated latency and are taking steps to stabilize. Expected partial relief in ~10-20m. Will update after next check."
raj-sales: AE on call responded: verbal approval to use burst for up to 4 GPUs for 2h if needed. They prefer we try evictions first.
mohit-platform: Scheduler relaxation finished pack, but still 2 fragmented GPUs remain. If load continues to climb, we'll need to either: a) manual burst of 4 GPUs (needs infra to allocate), or b) route some traffic to fallback model hosted in us-west-2. Manual burst command (requires infra): 
```
redwoodctl dedicated burst --tenant orchid-enterprise --gpus 4 --duration 2h --reason "production spike"
```
ari-oncall: Which will be faster? Manual burst or re-routing to hosted?
tessa-sre: Manual burst will give immediate headroom but requires infra ops to attach GPUs and update routing. Reroute to hosted fallback is config-only, quicker, but may have a 5-10% accuracy regression for some rerank cases.
ops-jen: Infra ops (me + infra) can do manual burst within ~8-12 minutes after approval. Who approves cost?
raj-sales: AE already ok for 4 GPUs/2h. You have the go-ahead.
mohit-platform: I'm coordinating with infra lead for actual attach. Logging the change in incident timeline.
customer-support: Customer on call wants to know if tokenization/PII is staying on-prem. If we route to hosted fallback we need to ensure sensitive traffic is excluded. Nina, please confirm what endpoints are safe to route.
nina-se: I'll validate: payments_rerank path cannot leave VPC. We'll only route non-payments traffic for now. I'll provide a traffic filter in 3m.
ari-oncall: Ok plan: (1) Evict best-effort (done) + placement relaxation (done). (2) If metrics stable in 10m, do nothing further. (3) If queue/503s persist, infra to attach 4 GPU burst (approved) and we update routing rules to share load. (4) If any sensitive endpoints affected, do hosted route only for non-sensitive paths.
tessa-sre: Adding monitoring dashboards & alert thresholds for the next 2h. Will post link.
mohit-platform: Infra attach started (ops-jen + infra-lead). ETA 9m.
ari-oncall: Noted spike: additional tenant background sync started 7m ago from orchidsvc-backfill job — asking customer engineering to stop non-critical syncs. Nina, can you ask them to pause?
nina-se: Messaging customer eng now: "Pause orchidsvc-backfill for 15m to reduce load while we stabilize."
customer-support: Customer confirmed pause. Great.
ops-jen: Infra attach complete. Executing burst attach: 
```
redwoodctl dedicated attach --pool orchid-enterprise --gpus 4 --temporary --owner incident-1849997777
```
ops-jen: Burst attach succeeded. Pool capacity now 68 GPUs (virtual burst).
ari-oncall: Immediate improvement: queue latency p95 -> 40ms, 503s near zero. Marking as mitigated.
tessa-sre: Keeping P1 until stable for 1 hour. Will create postmortem ticket and include recommended config changes: increase fragmentation tolerance, pre-authorize small bursts for this tenant, and add an automated emergency eviction policy.
raj-sales: Notifying AE and billing: we used 4 GPUs burst for ~2h window (will confirm duration).
mohit-platform: Recording config flips and burst commands in change-log. Will revert placement_relaxation flag after 30m if stable.
ari-oncall: Handoff: Tessa will own incident for next 2h monitoring, then postmortem. If anything regresses, page oncall immediately.
tessa-sre: Acknowledged, taking lead.
incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED • mitigations: evict_best_effort(8GPU), placement_relaxation=true, dedicated_burst(4GPU, temporary). Current state: mitigated. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled in #postmortems. Severity remains P1 until 1h stable.
ari-oncall: Thanks all. I'll update the support ticket and close this thread after stabilization window. :thumbsup:
ops-jen: leaving note: if we see repeated fragmentation events for orchid-enterprise we should consider dedicating contiguous nodes or increasing reserved contiguous slabs.
tessa-sre: Noted. Will add to postmortem runbook."
